rules.summary: BI-EUR belongs to core class I, which the prospectus limits to institutional investors. It defines these under art. 174 of the 2010 Law: credit institutions and other financial professionals investing for themselves or for other investors (including retail clients under a discretionary management agreement), insurance companies, pension funds and other UCIs. The prospectus class restriction is the binding hard rule. Transferees must also meet the eligibility rules.

rules.summary: Shares may not be offered or sold in the USA, and US persons may not subscribe unless the board or the management company decides otherwise. The definition is mixed. It is a residence- and organisation-based list (US residents, US partnerships and corporations, US agencies and branches, certain accounts and vehicles) plus any US person under Rule 902 of Regulation S. 'Non-United States persons' under CFTC Rule 4.7 are carved out. US citizenship or US tax status alone does not exclude: US taxpayers may subscribe as long as they are not US persons.

citations.quote: The shares in the SICAV may not be directly or indirectly offered or sold in the USA. Unless otherwise decided by the board or the management company, US persons may not subscribe for shares in the SICAV.
Therefore, US taxpayers, as defined for US federal income tax purposes, may subscribe for shares in the SICAV as long as they do not qualify as US persons.
a US resident, a trust of which a US resident is a trustee, or an estate of which a US resident is an executor or administrator
any other U.S. person defined by US Rule 902 of Regulation S

rules.summary: Jurisdictional restriction: investing is legal only where the shares are registered for public sale or where local law does not prohibit the sale. Some funds or classes may not be available in certain jurisdictions, so the desk must check the class's registration in the client's country.

citations.quote: Distributing this prospectus, offering these shares for sale, or investing in these shares is legal only where the shares are registered for public sale or where sale is not prohibited by local law or regulation.
Also, some funds or share classes that are available in certain jurisdictions may not be available in others.

rules.summary: AML/KYC gating: investors must provide documentary evidence of identity, beneficial owners, address and source of funds before an account is opened. The SICAV may delay or deny account opening and transactions until satisfactory documents are received. Intermediaries buying for clients are subject to enhanced due diligence.

citations.quote: We may delay or deny the opening of your account and any associated transaction requests and payments (including switches redemptions and transfers) until we receive, and judge to be satisfactory, all requested documents.

rules.summary: Discretionary rights: the SICAV may reject any subscription, and may soft-close (new investors) or hard-close (all investors) the fund or a class without notice. It may compulsorily redeem holders who are or may become ineligible. Investors suspected of market timing or excessive trading may have requests rejected. The board sets eligibility and ownership restrictions for each fund and class.

citations.quote: Reject or cancel any application to open an account or any request to subscribe for or transfer shares We can reject the entire amount or part of it.
A closure may apply only to new investors (soft closure) or to further investments from existing shareholders as well (hard closure).
We may therefore take various measures to protect shareholder interests, including rejecting, suspending or cancelling any request we believe represents excessive trading or market timing.
